newsitem.title: UK: LME implements first reform after Sumitomo.
newsitem.headline: LME implements first reform after Sumitomo.

text.p: The London Metal Exchange (LME) broke with around 118 years of tradition on Monday, allowing a LME staff member in to the trading ring to set prices, thus implementing the first reform since the Sumitomo copper affair.

Under the change, prompted by the Securities and Investments Board's (SIB) review of the LME after Sumitomo Corp lost $2.6 billion in copper trading, representatives of ring trading companies will no longer set official prices.
From Monday a committee comprising LME staff set the official prices, used around the world as benchmark prices, and the chairman of that committee sits in the trading ring.

Until now, only traders and the Lord Mayor of the City of London have been allowed in the trading area, a circular bench within which open-outcry trading occurs during four so-called "ring" sessions per day and two "kerb" sessions.
The change removes any appearance of a conflict of interest by trading companies which used to set prices and also have positions in the market.
Traders greeted the appearance of the staff member in the trading ring with smiles and one even jokingly gave him an order.
"It seemed a bit bizarre today with a new face in the ring, but it'll probably be better in the end," one floor trader said.
